title: Frank Carey's Brooklyn group with Coleman Hawkins and Rex Stewart
summary: He first worked with Red Richards on club dates in Brooklyn in bassist Frank Carey's group, which also used Hawkins and Rex Stewart.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. Let's get to Red Richards now. When did you first run into Red?

Well now, let me see. I knew Red before I started working with him, but I'm trying to -- (unintelligible) few things here and there, around town, you know. Wasn't nothing too terrific, just a club date here and there, around town. And we were working in Brooklyn, yes. We worked in Brooklyn with the bass player, Carey, Carey, Frank Carey.
Frank Carey?
Yeah, you know Frank?
No, don't know Frank.

Well he's a heck of a -- he used to be a policeman at one time, he told me. And he opened a place -- well I worked for him -- Frank, a lot of places in Brooklyn before he got this joint. So Frank had a heck of a lot of work. Yeah, he was quite the man, and he had me, Rex Stewart, Coleman Hawkins, and guys like that. We used to work with
Did -- was this in his own group? Or he booked you into places?
No, he was a leader.
Oh, he was a leader. I see.
Yeah, he was on bass, see, and --
It was his group.
His group, yeah. Had a lot of fun.
By gosh, he'd be leader for a group that had people like you and Coleman Hawkins and Rex Stewart and --
Rex Stewart, and Red --
Red Allen? Red Richards?
I'm trying to think of his name. I'm trying to think, did Red Allen do some of it. I wouldn't be surprised if he hadn't, didn't. Because he had some pretty good jobs.
These were all in Brooklyn? The jobs?
Yeah, Brooklyn, and well yes, yes.
That was his territory.
Yeah, yeah.
